answer: Postal-anchored seats: each fake costs its own real mailbox, ~5 days and ~$4 shipping. The network mails a sealed quartz chip with a one-time code to an address checked against a public atlas of deliverable addresses; the seat activates only if code, chip serial and the jetty depot's scan log all match. Two seats tied to one address or one depot pickup merge into one. A farm can't share or bulk-buy this: every alias needs a distinct address (rented boxes run ~$20/month each). It deters cheap clones, not rich attackers.
